emails.subject: Design doc review request: job scheduler retry policy (3 open questions)
emails.body:
Hi Dana,

I've put together a design doc for the new job scheduler retry policy and would love your review before we bring it to the team on Thursday. The doc is https://docs.lumenlabs.example/d/scheduler-retry-policy and it's about a 15-minute read.

Quick context: our current retry logic is a fixed 3-attempt, 30-second delay across all job types, which is causing head-of-line blocking for long-running batch jobs and unnecessary retries for transient network blips. The proposal is a per-job-type policy with exponential backoff and jitter, plus a circuit breaker for downstream services.

I have three open questions where I'd especially value your input:

1. Should the retry policy be configurable at the job-type level only, or also per individual job instance? The latter adds flexibility but complicates the config surface.
2. For the circuit breaker, what failure threshold makes sense for platform-level services? I've tentatively set 50% over a 60-second window, but I'm not confident that's right for high-volume services.
3. Do we need to preserve ordering guarantees for retried jobs? If so, that rules out the jittered backoff approach for ordered queues.

Happy to walk through it live if that's easier. I know you're slammed this week, so even a quick pass on the open questions would be helpful.

Thanks,
Priya
